questions.stem: A house increases in value from £200,000 to £230,000. What is the percentage increase?
questions.explanation: Increase = £30,000. Percentage increase = $\frac{30{,}000}{200{,}000} \times 100 = 15\%$. Always divide by the original value.

questions.stem: What decimal multiplier would you use to increase an amount by 8%?
questions.explanation: An 8% increase means you keep 100% and add 8%, giving 108% of the original. As a decimal multiplier: $1.08$.

questions.stem: £5000 is invested at 3% compound interest per year. What is the value after 2 years?
questions.explanation: After 1 year: $5000 \times 1.03 = £5150$. After 2 years: $5150 \times 1.03 = £5304.50$. With compound interest, you earn interest on previous interest.

questions.stem: After a 20% decrease, a price is £64. What was the original price?
questions.explanation: After a 20% decrease, £64 represents 80% of the original. So original $= \frac{64}{0.80} = £80$. To find the original, divide by the multiplier, not the percentage.
